quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #18
										  					
  

20 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT happen after drinking alcohol?

options.text: Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.
Your judgment of speed and distance becomes unclear.
You become less alert.
You calm down and can concentrate better.

questions.correctAnswerText: You calm down and can concentrate better.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time, reduces your ability to see clearly, changes how you judge speed and distance, reduces your recovery from headlight glare, and often makes you more likely to take risks.

questions.question: Can you drive around or under a railroad crossing gate that is moving up or down?

options.text: Yes, as long as no train is too close.
Yes, if your vehicle fits without hitting the gate.
Yes, if you look carefully in both directions first.
No, never.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, never.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights, lowered crossing gates, and bells at a railroad crossing mean you must stop completely. Do not cross the tracks until the lights and bells stop and the gates are fully raised. Never drive around or under a moving gate.

questions.question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Pump the brake pedal quickly several times.
Slow down gradually without using the brakes.
Press the brake pedal hard as quickly as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually without using the brakes.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat while driving, hold the steering wheel firmly and keep the vehicle straight. Take your foot off the accelerator and do not brake. Let the vehicle slow down on its own. Use the brakes gently only if needed. Pull off the road when safe.

questions.question: What is defensive driving?

options.text: Driving in an aggressive way.
Using safe driving strategies to prevent crashes.
More dangerous than regular driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using safe driving strategies to prevent crashes.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means using safe strategies to prevent crashes. You adjust your driving based on weather, how you feel, and the actions of other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians.

questions.question: At dusk or on overcast days, what should you do?

options.text: Use your four-way flashers.
Use your parking lights.
Do not turn on any lights.
Turn on your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your headlights.
questions.explanation: At dusk or on overcast days, turn on your headlights. Use low beam when within 1,000 feet of an oncoming vehicle and within 500 feet of a vehicle ahead of you. Always use low beams in bad weather.

questions.question: When should you use your horn?

options.text: When another vehicle is blocking your way.
When it may help prevent a crash.
When another driver makes a mistake.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it may help prevent a crash.
questions.explanation: Use your horn only when needed to avoid crashes. Do not use it to tell a slow driver to go faster or to get out of your way.

questions.question: When must you show proof of insurance to a police officer?

options.text: Only if you are in a crash.
If you are in a crash or stopped for a ticket.
Only if you are stopped and given a ticket.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you are in a crash or stopped for a ticket.
questions.explanation: You must carry proof of insurance whenever you drive. You must show your insurance and license to an officer when stopped for a traffic violation or after a crash.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and be ready to stop if cars are coming.
Come to a complete stop, then go when safe.
Drive carefully through the intersection without always stopping.
Stop only if there is traffic on the crossing road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop, then go when safe.
questions.explanation: A stop sign means you must stop completely and let vehicles and pedestrians at or heading toward the intersection go first. Go again when it is safe.

questions.question: What can cause "highway hypnosis"?

options.text: Looking straight ahead at the road for a long time.
Taking frequent breaks.
Getting too much sleep before driving.
Driving short distances on highways.

questions.correctAnswerText: Looking straight ahead at the road for a long time.
questions.explanation: Highway hypnosis happens when you look straight ahead at the road for long periods and stop checking ahead, behind, and around your vehicle. This can cause you to zone out and crash into traffic that is slowing or stopping.

questions.question: What happens to your field of vision when you increase your speed?

options.text: It increases.
It decreases.
You can see cross traffic better.
It does not change.

questions.correctAnswerText: It decreases.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive, the narrower your field of vision becomes. As you go faster and see less around you, you must watch carefully for hazards.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for bicycles.
Bicycles not allowed.
Bicycle repair shop ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for bicycles.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to areas where animals, people, and vehicles may cross the road.

questions.question: What does drinking coffee after drinking alcohol do?

options.text: Decreases blood alcohol concentration.
Cancels the effect of the alcohol.
Has no effect on blood alcohol concentration.
Increases blood alcohol concentration.

questions.correctAnswerText: Has no effect on blood alcohol concentration.
questions.explanation: Drinking coffee will not reduce your blood alcohol concentration. Coffee may help you stay awake, but it cannot change your blood alcohol level or make you sober.

questions.question: What should car drivers know about large trucks?

options.text: Have large blind spots.
Can stop more quickly than passenger vehicles.
Do not need more room to maneuver than passenger vehicles.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have large blind spots.
questions.explanation: Large trucks have big blind spots in front, on the sides, and in the rear. Avoid staying in these areas. Trucks need more space to turn and stop than passenger vehicles because of their size and weight.

questions.question: When can you drink alcohol in a vehicle on a public highway?

options.text: As long as you aren't driving.
If you are riding in the back seat.
If you are riding in the back of a pick-up truck.
Under no circumstances.

questions.correctAnswerText: Under no circumstances.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drink or have open alcohol in a vehicle on any public road or sidewalk. You cannot have an open bottle of alcohol in the main seating area of any vehicle on a public road.

questions.question: What should you do on slippery roads?

options.text: Slow down.
Drive more quickly.
Drive the speed limit, with caution.
Not drive more quickly than 20 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down when rain, snow, or sleet begins. These conditions make roads slippery. When road conditions are bad, you may need to drive slower than the posted speed limit for safety.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow arrow traffic signal, what should you do?

options.text: Should merge into a lane in the direction of the arrow.
Should come to a complete stop.
May turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Have the right-of-way and may expect oncoming traffic to stop for them.

questions.correctAnswerText: May turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow arrow means you can turn left in the direction of the arrow. However, oncoming traffic has a green light, so you must yield to them and to pedestrians.

questions.question: What does a single dashed yellow line separating traffic mean?

options.text: Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.
Both lanes travel in the same direction.
Drivers may not pass.
Drivers may pass, even if it could be dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A single dashed yellow line means drivers in both directions can pass. You may only pass if you will not interfere with oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What do two solid yellow lines on the road mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed for drivers from both directions.
Passing is not allowed.
Passing is allowed if you are at the top a hill.
Passing is allowed during daylight only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines show traffic moving in opposite directions. Never cross two solid yellow lines to pass, from either direction.

questions.question: What does this warning sign tell drivers?

options.text: The right lane is ending and traffic should merge left.
The road curves ahead.
There are upcoming intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane is ending and traffic should merge left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They tell you about conditions right ahead. This sign warns drivers that one lane is ending and traffic must move left.

questions.question: You exit the freeway on a ramp that curves downhill. What should you do?

options.text: Slow to a safe speed before the curve.
Slow to the posted speed limit for the freeway.
Wait until you have entered the curve to begin braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow to a safe speed before the curve.
questions.explanation: Always slow down before entering a curve. You cannot see hazards ahead clearly, and braking in a curve may cause your vehicle to skid.
